body.statement: Uniformly over the bounded radius regime \( (r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3 \) for which \(\mathcal M_n\) is nonempty and over the fixed reservoir-rich shell constants, with every minimax infimum taken over \(T\in\mathcal T_n\) measurable in the observed sample and allowed to use \(m_0\), \(m_1\), \(p\), and the certified radii, \(\mathfrak R_n^{(1)}\asymp\rho_n\), \(\mathfrak R_n^{(2)}\asymp\rho_n\), and \(\mathfrak R_{n,\delta}^{(\mathrm{prob})}\asymp\rho_n\) for every fixed \(\delta\in(0,\delta_0]\). Thus the same \(\rho_n\) is the sharp frontier for absolute risk, root mean-squared risk, and fixed-probability error.
body.proof_tex:
The upper and lower bounds use the same law--function class \(\mathcal M_n\)
and decision class \(\mathcal T_n\).  By
\texttt{thm:clipped-absolute-upper} and \texttt{def:absolute-risk},
\[
\mathfrak R_n^{(1)}
\leq\sup_{\mathcal M_n}E_P|
\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^\star}-\tau(P)|
\leq C\rho_n.                                             \tag{71}
\]

For \(n\geq5\), every block size \(m_j\) in
\texttt{def:median-estimator} satisfies \(n/9\leq m_j\leq n\).  Apply the
finite-sample inequality (12) from \texttt{thm:clipped-absolute-upper} on a
block at the common full-sample threshold \(\lambda_n^\star\).  Deterministic
bias terms are unchanged, and
\[
m_j^{-1/2}\leq3n^{-1/2},\quad\quad
m_j^{-1/(\kappa+1)}\leq9^{1/(\kappa+1)}n^{-1/(\kappa+1)},\quad\quad
(m_jr_{1n}^2)^{-1}\leq9(nr_{1n}^2)^{-1}.                  \tag{72}
\]
Thus the substitutions (13)--(18), with only fixed numerical changes, give
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}E_P|
\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^\star}^{(j)}-\tau(P)|\leq K\rho_n. \tag{73}
\]
Block independence follows from \texttt{ass:iid}.  Therefore
\texttt{lem:median-risk-upgrade} gives
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}
\left\{E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}-\tau(P))^2\right]\right\}^{1/2}
\leq\sqrt{21}\,K\rho_n.                                  \tag{74}
\]

It remains to check \(1\leq n<5\) without bounding \(g_0\), \(g_1\), or
\(Y\) separately.  In this range
\[
\lambda_n^\star\geq
\lambda_{\min}:=\min\{\lambda_0,4^{-1/(\kappa+1)}\}>0,
\quad\quad1-p^\circ\geq\eta_+/2.                              \tag{75}
\]
Use the exact identity (5) with
\(\Delta=g_1-g_0\), \(h_a=m_a-g_a\), and the arm-specific residuals.  The
triangle inequality, the signal moment, the public regression certificates,
and the conditional residual variances imply
\[
\begin{split}
\|\psi_{\lambda_n^\star}\|_{P,2}
\leq{}&\sqrt M+r_{1n}+r_{0n}
+\lambda_{\min}^{-1}\sqrt{2(\sigma_1^2+r_{1n}^2)}\\
&+{2\over\eta_+}\sqrt{2(\sigma_0^2+r_{0n}^2)}
\leq C_0.
\end{split}                                                   \tag{76}
\]
For example,
\[
E_P\!\left[{D(\varepsilon_1-h_1)^2\over q_{\lambda_n^\star}^2}\right]
\leq {2(\sigma_1^2+r_{1n}^2)\over\lambda_{\min}^2},
\]
and the analogous control expression is at most
\(8(\sigma_0^2+r_{0n}^2)/\eta_+^2\).  Also
\(|\tau(P)|\leq\|\Delta\|_{P,2}\leq\sqrt M\).  Convexity of the square gives
\[
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^\star}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\leq {1\over n}\sum_{i=1}^nE_P\!\left[(\psi_{\lambda_n^\star}(O_i)-\tau(P))^2\right]
\leq C_1^2.                                               \tag{77}
\]
Since \(\rho_n\geq n^{-1/2}\geq1/2\), (77) is at most
\((2C_1\rho_n)^2\).  This proves the root-MSE upper bound for the full-sample
fallback using only \(M\), \(\bar r\), \(\sigma_0^2\), \(\sigma_1^2\),
\(\lambda_{\min}\), and \(\eta_+\).  The median rule belongs to
\(\mathcal T_n\), so the corrected \texttt{def:root-mse-risk} gives
\(\mathfrak R_n^{(2)}\leq C\rho_n\) for every \(n\).

For fixed \(\delta\in(0,1/4)\), the deviation conclusion of
\texttt{thm:clipped-absolute-upper} and \texttt{def:probability-risk} give
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,\delta}^{(\mathrm{prob})}\leq C_\delta\rho_n. \tag{78}
\]
Conversely, \texttt{thm:four-channel-converse} gives both loss lower bounds and
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}P\{|T-\tau(P)|\geq c\rho_n\}\geq2\delta_0
\quad\text{for every }T\in\mathcal T_n.                   \tag{79}
\]
If \(0<\delta\leq\delta_0\) and \(u<c\rho_n\), then
\[
\sup_{\mathcal M_n}P\{|T-\tau(P)|>u\}
\geq2\delta_0>\delta.                                  \tag{80}
\]
Taking the two infima in \texttt{def:probability-risk} proves its lower bound.
Equations (71)--(80) and the two loss lower bounds prove all three uniform
equivalences.  The converse uses the reservoir-rich shell class; the upper
bounds used only the broader uniform-shell conditions.
body.justification: It matches the feasible clipped and median estimators to the four-channel converse for absolute loss, actual mean-squared loss, and fixed-probability error.
body.gap: The closest regular-overlap results provide source-class lower-bound forms, while accepted policy-regret and continuous-exposure frontiers have non-nested targets and classes.
body.consumer: Method developers can use \(\rho_n\) as the oracle benchmark without conflating full-ATE estimation with policy regret or continuous-exposure clamp estimation.
